# Cargo Standard Operating Procedure
This procedure applies to the Quartermaster, Cargo Technicians, Salvage Specialists, and any crew member acting in a logistics capacity.
## Requisitions and Approval
Logistics fills requests from the whole station. Orders [italic]should[/italic] be filled in the order received, with departmental necessities taking priority over personal and novelty items.
An order that names a requesting crew member and a reason [italic]should[/italic] be approved as routine. Unattributed orders for restricted goods [italic]should[/italic] be held until the requester is identified.
[italic]A Doctor ordering medical supplies is routine. An unsigned order for a crate of weapons is not.[/italic]
The Quartermaster has final say within the department. Command may override a refusal, but [italic]should[/italic] state why on the record.
## Restricted and Contraband Orders
Weapons, armour, and anything on the contraband list [bold]shall not[/bold] be ordered without approval from the Head of Security, Warden, or Commanding Officer. Approved weapon shipments [bold]must[/bold] be handed directly to Security, not left on the loading dock.
Anything requiring paperwork under [textlink="Permits" link="GuidePermits"] requires that paperwork [italic]before[/italic] the crate is opened, not after.
Logistics [bold]shall not[/bold] sell, gift, or trade station-critical equipment or another department's property without that department's consent.
## Budget and Spending
The station budget is a shared resource. Logistics [italic]should not[/italic] exhaust it on a single department's requests, on bulk luxury goods, or on personal purchases.
Spending that would leave the station unable to fund emergency supplies requires the Quartermaster's approval, and for large sums, Command's.
Selling station property for profit — airlocks, wall panels, the department's own equipment — is theft, not enterprise.
## Bounties
Bounties are the department's primary income and [italic]should[/italic] be worked steadily rather than in a rush at shift's end.
Cargo Technicians [italic]should[/italic] ask other departments for bounty items rather than taking them. Departments are encouraged to cooperate, but Logistics has no authority to compel them.
## Salvage and Expeditions
Salvage Specialists [bold]shall not[/bold] depart without functioning breathing equipment and a means of returning. Expeditions [italic]should[/italic] be logged so that Command knows who is off-station and when they are due back.
Salvagers [italic]should[/italic] request specialised tools — insulated gloves, welding goggles, and similar — from Engineering, which is obliged to provide them. See [textlink="Engineering SOP" link="GuideEngineeringSOP"].
Hostile creatures and artefacts recovered from wrecks [bold]shall not[/bold] be brought aboard alive or active. Anomalous recoveries go to Epistemics — see [textlink="Science SOP" link="GuideEpistemicsSOP"].
Salvage wrecks and expedition sites are not private property. Loot recovered on station time belongs to the station, and [italic]should[/italic] be turned in or sold rather than hoarded.
## Shuttle and Dock Discipline
The cargo shuttle is departmental equipment. It [bold]shall not[/bold] be used for personal transport, for smuggling crew off-station, or for evacuating during an emergency in place of the evacuation shuttle.
The loading dock [italic]should[/italic] be kept clear. Crates left in the airlock path are a hazard during a breach.
## Departmental Conduct
Logistics [italic]should not[/italic] run protection rackets, artificial shortages, or price gouging on goods the station has already paid for. Trading favours is fine; extortion is not.
The Quartermaster is responsible for the department's spending and for the conduct of its workers, and answers to the Commanding Officer for both.
